Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

Alright, now let's try some problems on Taylors and McLaren series.

Key details

  • As I was mentioning in the lecture, we are not going to solve problems on the Taylors and McLaren series for a function of single variable.
  • But we'll try.
  • And find out the Taylor series and the McLaren series for a function of two independent variables.
  • So the first question is expand e power x cos y in powers of x minus 1 and y minus 4 up to second degree term.
  • So the point is 1 comma pi by 4 because we want to express it in that form.
  • x minus 1 into f x of 1 comma pi by four plus y minus pi by four into f y of 1 comma 5 by 4.
  • So this is only the first degree term.
  • The question says up to the second degree term.
  • So the next one will be plus x minus 1 the whole square.
  • And then plus etc.
  • Of course, it's an infinite series.
  • But what we are required to find is I need to calculate what is the value of the function.
  • The function is e power x into cos y.
  • And then we will find all the partial derivatives of this, or till whatever we require and the corresponding values.
  • F of 1 is e and a cos of pi by 4 is root 2.
  • Then what is f x of x y?
  • F x of x y is you have to treat cos y as constant.
  • What will be f y of x y now?
  • I need to differentiate cos y by treating x as constant.
  • Now we are done with the first order partial derivatives.
  • F xx of x comma y will be I need to differentiate this again with respect to x.
  • I need to differentiate fx with respect to y.
  • And the last one that I need is f y f y of x comma y.
  • So that means I need to differentiate f y with respect to y again.
  • If you observe carefully, all these values are same and only thing they differ is because of the sign.

Example or application from the lecture

  • So first let's write out what is the Taylor series expansion.
  • And then now let's find the mixed second order partial derivative fxy of x y.
  • That's because of the point that they have given about which we need to expand the function.

Core explanation · 05:00–09:59

I can write f of x comma y as f of 1 comma pi by 4 is e pi root 2.

Key details

  • So in fact I can take out e by root two common from all the terms because every term here has e by root 2.
  • Next one is x minus 1.
  • Plus, for y it is minus, so y minus y by four.
  • This is the second degree term.
  • Plus I have x minus one the whole square by two factorial.
  • F x is positive.
  • and minus x minus one of course into two into y minus pi by four divided by two factorial and the last term is also minus I'll get y minus pi by four the whole square divided by two factorial.
  • So I can stop here for now because they have asked me to expand only up till the second degree term.
  • So maybe in the next problem we'll see an expansion for Taylor series or McLaren series wherein we go up to third degree term.
  • F of x y is equal to log of two x plus y plus one about the point zero comma zero up to three terms.
  • That's a question.
  • F x at zero coma zero by two factorial plus two x y.
  • f x y 0 comma zero by two factorial plus f y at zero comma zero into y square by two factorial and then of course plus etcetera other terms will continue.
  • I'll get log of 1, which is 0 for me.
  • So first term, the constant term is not there for this particular function.
  • f x will be 1 by 2x plus y plus 1 into 2.
  • Because I am differentiating with respect to x, I need to treat the other two variables as constant.
  • What will be FY of X, comma Y.
  • If y is again 1 by 2x plus y plus 1 and the derivative of y is just 1.
  • So f y of x comma y or 0 will be just 1 because these two terms goes to 0.
  • So that means f x at 0 comma 0 will be minus 4.
  • But let me find the two more terms, which is fx y.
  • of x y so that I can complete all the second degree term.
  • And the last one would be to calculate f y of x y.

Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

Will be the first term is 0.

Key details

  • Okay, that's the first term.
  • Minus 4x square by 2 factorial.
  • Minus 2xy by 2 factorial.
  • Actually these two terms were not necessary because the question says up to three terms.
  • Two x plus y plus one will be two x minus or plus y minus two x square, okay, minus x y minus y square by two plus x.
  • So the next problem we'll see it as an application of Taylor series.
  • Now in the next problem we'll see how to apply this Taylor series to evaluate a value.
  • This is the question, right?
  • So that means just observe these values.
  • Because I want the approximate value, can I say that f of 0.9 and minus 1.2 is approximately equal to f of 1 comma minus 1.
  • And then so f x at 1 comma minus 1 will be you substitute y as minus 1 and this is square which is 2.
  • Next is we'll find out what is f y of x comma y.
  • But for now I think because we have three non zero terms, this should be sufficient.
  • That means we got tan inverse of x y.
  • I can write tan inverse of x y as minus pi by four plus I'm expanding about the point x minus one so x minus one into minus half plus y plus one into plus half.
  • Plus, etcetera of course.
  • But this also can give a better close approximation of this.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let's try another problem on find Taylor series expansion of f of x y equal to tan inverse of x y and find the approximate value of f of zero point nine comma minus one point two.

Core explanation · 15:00–19:59

0.9 and minus 1.2 will be minus 5 by 4.

Key details

  • And if you substitute here for x is 0.9, minus 1 will be just 0.1 with a minus into minus half.
  • Plus y is minus one point two plus one will be again minus zero point one minus zero point two in fact.
  • Minus 0.1 by 2 is just the 1 by 20.
  • This is just an application problem of how we can use the Taylor series to evaluate a function at a particular point.
